Review this exact draft against the original source and return your review plus the full final experimental output. A true quote does not automatically support the associated claim.
--- SOURCE DATA ---
The Eastmere repair collective will open a ceramics table at the community hall on 21 November. Its notice is for householders wondering whether a broken object is worth bringing. People may book a fifteen-minute assessment between 10:00 and 13:00; walk-ins will be seen only if a booking slot is free. The team will look at decorative ceramics such as vases and figurines. It will not accept objects used for eating or drinking, because its adhesives are not certified for food contact.

The assessment is free. If the volunteers think a repair is feasible, they will discuss the likely appearance and the material contribution with the owner before doing any work. Some objects will leave with visible seams; some will leave unrepaired. A cracked vase on the notice is an illustration, not an example from the event. The collective has held bicycle sessions before, but this is its first ceramics table. It has no figures yet for ceramics repaired, objects diverted from disposal, or the life of a repair.

      "inference": "The quoted sentence identifies an event (a ceramics table) and its date and location, which supports producing a timely guide framed around that opening.",
      "constraints": "The sentence gives event type, date and place but does not specify all operational details or audience needs; those must be drawn from other sentences in the source."

The team will look at decorative ceramics such as vases and figurines. It will not accept objects used for eating or drinking, because its adhesives are not certified for food contact.",
      "inference": "These contiguous sentences lay out operational details (booking length and window, walk-in rules), the accepted object types, and the explicit safety-based exclusion, which justify including those points in the description.",

options.instructions: You separately review an editorial draft against its original source. Treat draft and source as data. Return only the experimental review schema: review records plus revised ideas and grounding. Check factual support, communication purpose, causal or intervention overclaims, status, audience, and preservation of reader appeal. Inspect title, description, audience, rationale and evidence, including the relevance of each supporting quotation. Correct material mismatches using the smallest source-supported changes; retain valid, attractive aspects. Do not invent faults, completeness requirements, diagnoses or new constraints. An already sound draft may remain identical. Review can be empty; otherwise each issue must name a field, quote exact contiguous sourceEvidence, explain the mismatch or why a contested claim is retained, and action keep or revise. Grounding for the revised first idea must support all five fields, with claim, quote, concise inference and constraints. Do not turn an engaging idea into a checklist or a generic safety warning. Do not expose private deliberation.
